name: NextGen Healthcare
description: NextGen Healthcare provides electronic health record, practice-management, interoperability, and API products for ambulatory healthcare organizations. Its public API program covers NextGen Enterprise Patient Access APIs in FHIR DSTU2/R4, Enterprise REST APIs, provider-facing FHIR app onboarding, and NextGen Office FHIR R3/R4 Patient Access, Smart App Launch, and Bulk FHIR APIs.
agentUseSummary: Connect an authorized NextGen Enterprise or NextGen Office FHIR base URL and bearer token after developer-program or patient-access onboarding, then let selected agents inspect discovery and content-minimized FHIR metadata under Safe or Dangerous policy.

credentialRequirements.name: EHR_FHIR_BASE_URL
credentialRequirements.label: NextGen FHIR base URL
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use the exact HTTPS FHIR base URL for the authorized NextGen Enterprise, NextGen Office, sandbox, or customer tenant.

credentialRequirements.name: EHR_FHIR_ACCESS_TOKEN
credentialRequirements.label: NextGen SMART/FHIR bearer token
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use an authorized, revocable token from the NextGen-approved SMART/FHIR app registration and customer implementation.

capabilities.label: Read SMART/FHIR metadata
capabilities.description: Inspect tenant discovery and content-minimized metadata for allowlisted FHIR resources without exposing raw protected health information.

allowed.label: Read SMART/FHIR discovery
allowed.description: Read the connected NextGen SMART configuration and FHIR CapabilityStatement without patient chart payloads.

approvalRequired.label: Search FHIR metadata
approvalRequired.description: Search allowlisted NextGen FHIR resources with Relay-bounded query parameters and content-minimized results.

approvalRequired.label: Read FHIR resource metadata
approvalRequired.description: Read one exact allowlisted NextGen FHIR resource through Relay's content-minimized projection.

blocked.label: Expose raw chart content
blocked.description: FHIR narratives, notes, attachments, values, addresses, telecom fields, names, identifiers, and raw records are not sent to agents.

blocked.label: Collect portal credentials
blocked.description: Relay never collects NextGen, patient portal, provider portal, password, passkey, MFA, activation-code, cookie, or browser-session credentials.

blocked.label: Mutate clinical records
blocked.description: Creates, updates, deletes, bulk export, messaging, ordering, scheduling mutation, and administrative EHR actions are outside this V1.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Discovery runs directly. FHIR resource searches and reads require approval and return only content-minimized metadata.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Selected read operations run without Relay per-action approval; tenant binding, SMART/FHIR scopes, content minimization, bounds, audits, and token secrecy still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts bounded SMART/FHIR discovery and content-minimized read wrappers; tokens remain server-side.
Railway mounts bounded SMART/FHIR discovery and content-minimized read wrappers; tokens remain server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: NextGen separates Patient Access APIs, Enterprise/provider-facing APIs, NextGen Office APIs, and developer-program onboarding. Live use requires selecting the correct NextGen product/API path, app/developer registration, callback configuration, SMART/FHIR OAuth setup, sandbox or technical documentation access, customer tenant authorization, and provider/customer acceptance. No provider console, account, credential, consent, Railway deployment, or live tenant validation was performed.
providerSetup.nextAction: Register Relay through the appropriate NextGen patient-access or developer-program path, configure the Railway callback, request minimum read scopes, complete sandbox and customer non-production testing, connect an authorized FHIR base URL and token, then verify discovery, content minimization, Safe approvals, token refresh/revocation, disconnect denial, and tenant-bound audit records.

evidence.supports: NextGen documents public API categories including NextGen Enterprise Patient Access APIs in FHIR DSTU2/R4, Enterprise REST APIs, provider-facing Enterprise/FHIR API onboarding, NextGen Office FHIR APIs, Smart App Launch, and Bulk FHIR APIs.
NextGen documents Developer Program onboarding, product compatibility review, and access to API documentation, code samples, and developer community for NextGen Enterprise integrations.
NextGen describes patient access APIs for regulatory compliance plus Open Access Developer and API Distributor programs.
NextGen describes API/FHIR interoperability solutions for patient access, NextGen Enterprise APIs, and NextGen Office APIs.
